A friend of mine and I are planning to write a mobile app for keeping track of your character stuff at the table. We've trolled the app store and haven't found anything that seems worthwhile for 5e (the best we found is RPG Scribe, which is optimized for 3.5e, or Sheet Yourself which is $5. Let me know if we missed a good one), so we figured we'd just do it ourselves. Plus, every programmer can use more side mobile app projects, right?

My question to you all: other than being able to track your numbers/inventory/spells/feats/etc on the fly, what features should we include?

Cool idea, I play 5e and would like to see an app like this! Just running some ideas by you:

  • sub tab for character sheets of pets or shapeshift form for druid

  • an easy way to track your spells used, arrows fired etc

  • character journal to write in as you play to log your progress, imortant names, quests goals etc so you wouldn't need pen and paper at all, just the app.

You can also add things that a normal character sheet doesn't have, like:

  • some sort of alarm clock that keeps track of how long you are playing and when to get up and walk around a little (sitting for hours straight is bad)

  • built in dices

  • maybe even a sound box with tavern background noises, owlbear howls, etc (that would annoy the crap out of me, but some people might like it).

  • Maybe a photo function so you can photograph drawn maps and save them.

  • And ofcourse: a way to save the info as file so you can always print it later or send it to your dm or something.

  • You can even make groups or social functions in it with linked accounts so the dm can give gold or xp to the entire group and their character sheets get updated?

Having dice rollers, with a toggle for advantage/disadvantage for the rolls, with a timeline of all rolls (that can be cleared).

I like to implement house rules a lot, which ends up with certain scores not being correct for specific types of stats (like proficiency). Please add a "Default" mode and a "Modify" mode, that allows you to either use the default stats/skills for that level and the ability to modify the numbers later on.

Have a list of all the actions available, what the result of such an action would be, and any current modifiers to that action. Selecting that action from the list opens a window that describes the action and showing the above information, along with a dice roller for the relevant action. For example, from a list, there is the "Attack" action along with everything else. It says you have 2 attacks, with several options for those attacks (shortsword, bow, unarmed), along with relevant modifiers for those attacks (have a toggle for Finesse to keep things simple), a d20 roller for attack and separate damage dice for each possible attack.

Highlight terms for things that modify them (underlined things are from feats, bold things are from class/racial effects, italics is from a temporary/magical effect), and when you click on something (like health) it displays all of the things that are modifying it (like the Toughness feat, constitution modifier, and hit die rolls).

Players tend to forget that they get bonuses to certain actions (like Dashing with the Mobile feat), and this can be a nice reminder of all the little things they might be missing out on (being able to ignore difficult terrain).

A full-on example:

A player wants to attack. Among his list of actions, his "Attack" action is highlighted as both being bold and underlined, bold stating that it is modified by his race/class effects (like Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting) and underlined because of his feat (Dual Wield).

Clicking on the attack action will show how many attacks he gets (can be modified in Modify mode, mostly just a placeholder for people to review from), each type of attack he has available (like Longbow and Shortsword), and each type of attack has a toggle for Finesse, swapping the stats from strength to dexterity. Clicking on the attack type will show you what causes what modifiers are caused from what (with a box to add/subtract modifiers at DM's discretion), and a toggle will be available to make it an "offhand" attack, which considers the changes from his fighting style and feats.

Additionally, there is both an "Attack" and "Hit" box. Clicking on the "Attack" box of that particular attack will show all of the modifiers effecting that roll, as well as a d20 roller. On the same screen, a shortcut to the "Hit" box is available (to prevent having people to go to the previous screen) for when the attack connects, which automatically rolls the damage for you.
